title: 2024 ADA Standards of Medical Care in Diabetes

diagnosis.content: Diabetes diagnosis: A1c ≥6.5%, FPG ≥126 mg/dL, or 2-hour PG ≥200 mg/dL during OGTT.
key_points: Screen annually if risk factors present

treatment.content: Metformin is first-line unless contraindicated. Add agents based on comorbidities and patient factors.
key_points: Metformin: First-line, start 500mg and titrate to 2000mg daily
GLP-1 RA: Add if ASCVD, HF, or CKD present - proven CV benefit
SGLT2i: Add if HF or CKD - proven renal and cardiac protection
DPP-4i: Alternative if GLP-1/SGLT2i not tolerated
Insulin: Add if A1c >10% or significant hyperglycemia symptoms

special_populations.ckd: Avoid metformin if eGFR <30. Prefer GLP-1 RA or SGLT2i for renal protection
special_populations.cvd: GLP-1 RA with proven CV benefit (liraglutide, semaglutide, dulaglutide)

monitoring.content: Monitor A1c every 3 months until target achieved, then every 6 months.

examples.metformin: Start 500mg daily with dinner, increase by 500mg weekly. Max 2000mg daily. Take with food.
examples.semaglutide: Start 0.25mg SC weekly x 4 weeks, then 0.5mg weekly. Titrate to 1mg if needed.
examples.empagliflozin: Start 10mg daily, increase to 25mg if tolerated. Monitor for genital infections.
